physicalNotes: Radius 0.17129122 Jupiter radii from Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract): 12,246 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 0.01636103 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): P 7.1027268 d
sources.shape: Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0576 au and stellar radius 0.512 solar radii; Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): inclination 89.6 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): transit mid-time 2458547.11249 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 15 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
